expectedMisconceptions: Children sometimes measure first and then quietly adjust their 'estimate' to look more accurate — encourage writing the estimate down before any tool touches the object, even if it turns out to be wrong.
A close estimate isn't the same as a correct process — the point of the table is comparing honestly, not getting the 'right' number.
stretchQuestions: Were your estimates closer for some kinds of objects than others? Why might that be?
If you had to teach someone else to estimate well, what would you tell them to look at first?
estimatedSupervision: Light to moderate — gathering a few household measuring tools beforehand helps the session flow; the estimating and table-drawing itself needs little supervision once set up.
